24.0.0.en: 1 Again in the ninth year, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 “Son of man, write thee the name of the day, even of this same day: the king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem this same day. 3 And utter a parable unto the rebellious house, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Set on a pot, set it on, and also pour water into it: 4 Gather the pieces thereof into it, even every good piece, the thigh, and the shoulder; fill it with the choice bones. 5 Take the choice of the flock, and burn also the bones under it, and make it boil well, and let them seethe the bones of it therein. 6 Wherefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose scum is therein, and whose scum is not gone out of it! bring it out piece by piece; let no lot fall upon it. 7 For her blood is in the midst of her; she set it upon the top of a rock; she poured it not upon the ground, to cover it with dust; 8 That it might cause fury to come up to take vengeance; I have set her blood upon the top of a rock, that it should not be covered. 9 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe to the bloody city! I will even make the pile for fire great. 10 Heap on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh, and spice it well, and let the bones be burned. 11 Then set it empty upon the coals thereof, that the brass of it may be hot, and may burn, and that the filthiness of it may be molten in it, that the scum of it may be consumed. 12 She hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her: her scum shall be in the fire. 13 In thy filthiness is lewdness: because I have purged thee, and thou wast not purged, thou shalt not be purged from thy filthiness any more, till I have caused my fury to rest upon thee. 14 I the LORD have spoken it: it shall come to pass, and I will do it; I will not go back, neither will I spare, neither will I repent; according to thy ways, and according to thy doings, shall they judge thee, saith the Lord GOD.”

24.0.1.en: The Lord specified to the prophet Ezekiel the ninth year of the reign of Jehoiachin, in the tenth month, on the tenth day, as the day of Nebuchadnezzar’s approach to Jerusalem. The Lord asked him to record this date in his notes, and it came in exact agreement with the date of the final siege of Jerusalem (2 Kgs 25:1), as though the Lord wanted to declare that what was happening was neither the product of chance nor a human plan, but events taking place by divine permission, according to a plan arranged at a precise time.

24.1.0.en: The Lord asked Ezekiel to utter a parable to “the rebellious house” [3], which would soon become a ruined and destroyed house. He likened Jerusalem to a pot filled with rust (verdigris), in which were gathered pieces of flesh, “every good piece, the thigh, and the shoulder,” and which was to be filled with the choice bones, so that it might boil and the bones be seethed in the midst of it. And the words of the Lord were: “Woe to the bloody city, to the pot whose scum is therein, and whose scum is not gone out of it! bring it out piece by piece; let no lot fall upon it... Heap on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh, and spice it well, and let the bones be burned. Then set it empty upon the coals thereof, that the brass of it may be hot, and may burn, and that the filthiness of it may be molten in it, that the scum of it may be consumed” [6-11].

24.1.1.en: He saw Jerusalem as a pot with the fire blazing under it, as the prophet Jeremiah had seen it before (Jer 1:13). But this is contrary to the understanding held by the leaders of the people, when they thought that Jerusalem was the pot that protects the flesh inside it, so that no one can come near to it as long as it is inside the pot (Ex 11:3); for they thought that Jerusalem would remain a wall of bronze protecting those within it, and that God would defend her whatever the circumstances, because she is His city. Here the prophet Ezekiel declares the opposite: she is the pot under which God pours out the fire of His wrath because of its rust, that is, its corruption. The fire refers to the bitterness of captivity and the destruction of those in her by divine command, for the Lord says to the Chaldeans: “Heap on wood, kindle the fire.” She had increased exceedingly in her evil, and therefore needed many fires to discipline her.

24.1.2.en: As for the placing of water with the pieces inside the pot, it is a reference to the state of slackness to which Judah, leaders and people, had come. All had become like water, without strength or power, all of it softness!

24.1.3.en: As for the placing of the choice pieces of the thigh and the shoulders with the bones, it is a reference to the fact that the great and the responsible do not escape, just as the people do not escape. All fall under the fire, and are brought out piece by piece, and no lot falls upon them, a sign that all leave the city with no regard for anyone’s dignity or abilities or resources; all are scattered in a foreign land without order. Jerusalem is emptied of her people, and destroyed in order to be cleansed from her multiplying rust, since idol worship had entered the temple of the Lord and His holy places, on every high place on the mountains and hills, as in the valleys and on the banks of the river, and under every green tree!

24.1.4.en: It is a terrible picture of Jerusalem blazing with fire, yet not without purpose. For St. Jerome sees in this a return to reform, saying: [The putting of flesh in the pot means that sinners become gentle. Their hardness is changed and they turn toward God, and their stony hearts become hearts of flesh... O what great mercy! O what a great mystery! The pieces of flesh are put in the pot so that the heart of man may melt and know that He is the Lord!]

24.2.0.en: 15 Also the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 16 “Son of man, behold, I take away from thee the desire of thine eyes with a stroke: yet neither shalt thou mourn nor weep, neither shall thy tears run down. 17 Forbear to cry, make no mourning for the dead, bind the tire of thine head upon thee, and put on thy shoes upon thy feet, and cover not thy lips, and eat not the bread of men. 18 So I spake unto the people in the morning: and at even my wife died; and I did in the morning as I was commanded. 19 And the people said unto me, Wilt thou not tell us what these things are to us, that thou doest so? 20 Then I answered them, The word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 21 Speak unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the excellency of your strength, the desire of your eyes, and that which your soul pitieth; and your sons and your daughters whom ye have left shall fall by the sword. 22 And ye shall do as I have done: ye shall not cover your lips, nor eat the bread of men. 23 And your tires shall be upon your heads, and your shoes upon your feet: ye shall not mourn nor weep; but ye shall pine away for your iniquities, and mourn one toward another. 24 Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign: according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord GOD. 25 Also, thou son of man, shall it not be in the day when I take from them their strength, the joy of their glory, the desire of their eyes, and that whereupon they set their minds, their sons and their daughters, 26 That he that escapeth in that day shall come unto thee, to cause thee to hear it with thine ears? 27 In that day shall thy mouth be opened to him which is escaped, and thou shalt speak, and be no more dumb: and thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the LORD.”

24.2.1.en: This is the conclusion of God’s declarations to the prophet Ezekiel concerning the final captivity of Judah and the destruction of the city. It reached its peak when the divine command came to him that his wife would die, and that he should declare this to the men of Judah, and shed no tear for her, and make no mourning, and utter no word of sorrow; that he should bind his turban, put on his shoes, not cover his lips, and not eat the bread of men, though this wife was the desire of his eyes! And indeed he spoke to the people thus, and in the evening his wife died, so that he carried out everything he had been commanded on the following day.

24.2.2.en: It is a terrifying picture of the destruction of the people, the beloved bride of God, yet there is no one who weeps or sheds a single tear because of the deadly intensity of grief; the tongue stops speaking and the tears dry up, and a man is swallowed up by inward sorrow and becomes like one in a stupor.

24.2.3.en: This was indeed fulfilled, and it was the last arrow to strike the prophet Ezekiel, in that he became a sign to them (24, 27)... He sighs in bitterness within himself and cannot speak; he refused to accept the bread of men, that is, the bread of mourning, since the people of the East were accustomed to send food to the house of mourning for them to eat... He would accept neither satisfaction from a human hand nor consolation from a man!

24.2.4.en: He made no mourning for his wife, because there is no one in Jerusalem to weep for her slain and those driven out of her. As for his binding the turban, putting on shoes, and not covering his lips, it is a sign that there is no room to remain at home in mourning... All go out and flee; there is no one to weep for the dead! Finally, the death of his wife took place in the evening, in the darkness, a sign of their unreadiness for these events despite the continual divine warnings through the prophets.

24.2.6.en: * You likened Your people to flesh in a pot with rust; the fires blaze in vain, because the flesh becomes cooked, but poisoned!

24.2.7.en: * Allow me, O Lord, to benefit from the fire of Your discipline; remove from my heart the rust of sin, and pull out the roots of poison from my depths; then I shall benefit from the fires of Your discipline, and become useful food!

24.2.8.en: * You allowed Your prophet’s wife to die, the desire of his eyes whom he loved, yet he does not weep for her nor accept consolation for her from a man!

24.2.9.en: She died in the evening, in the midst of the darkness; so my most precious soul dies, dies in the midst of the darkness of sin. I do not seek consolation from men, but I seek Your help and Your consolation; You alone are able to raise her from the darkness of her tomb, and make her a holy temple for Your Holy Spirit!

25.0.0.en: 1 The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying, 2 “Son of man, set thy face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them; 3 And say unto the Ammonites, Hear the word of the Lord GOD; Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned; and against the land of Israel, when it was desolate; and against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity; 4 Behold, therefore I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and they shall set their palaces in thee, and make their dwellings in thee: they shall eat thy fruit, and they shall drink thy milk. 5 And I will make Rabbah a stable for camels, and the Ammonites a couchingplace for flocks: and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 6 For thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thou hast clapped thine hands, and stamped with the feet, and rejoiced in heart with all thy despite against the land of Israel; 7 Behold, therefore I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and will deliver thee for a spoil to the heathen; and I will cut thee off from the people, and I will cause thee to perish out of the countries: I will destroy thee; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD.

25.0.1.en: The Ammonites are of the offspring of Ben-ammi, the son of Lot (Gen 19:38). They were hard of heart, offering their children as sacrifices to the god Milcom (1 Kgs 11:5-33), and they also worshipped Chemosh, the god of the Moabites, in the days of Jephthah (Judg 11:24). They allied themselves with the Moabites against the children of Israel; therefore God decreed against them that none of them should enter into the congregation of the Lord until the tenth generation (Deut 23:3).

25.0.2.en: They were in constant war with them (1 Sam 11:1-10; 2 Sam 12:26-31; 2 Chr 20:1; 2 Kgs 24:2). When Judah fell under the Babylonian captivity, the king of Babylon set Gedaliah over Jerusalem as governor on his behalf, and he began to gather the remnant of the Jews; then Baalis, king of the Ammonites, sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah and he killed him in order to scatter the Jews (Jer 40-41). They always mocked the Jews and derided them in their captivity, and therefore the prophet Jeremiah threatened them with destruction (Jer 49:1-6), as did Amos (Amos 2:13-15) and Zephaniah (Zeph 2:8, 11). They opposed Nehemiah in the building of the wall after the captivity (Neh 4:3, 7). Finally the Jews fought them in the time of the Maccabees, and their history gradually came to an end in the Greek and Roman periods, and the city of Amman was built on the remains of their capital Rabbah of Ammon.

25.1.0.en: The Lord asked the prophet Ezekiel to set his face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them [2], as though he represents God, for “the face of the LORD is against them that do evil, to cut off the remembrance of them from the earth” (Ps 34:16). If the Lord declared His chastisements against Israel, it was for their repentance; but as for the Ammonites, who represent the sin of pride, God sets His face against it to destroy it.

25.2.0.en: The Ammonites represent the sin of pride, which is the first of the vices, for He says: “Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary... Because thou hast clapped thine hands, and stamped with the feet, and rejoiced in heart with all thy despite against the land of Israel...” [3-6]. She stood in arrogance, boasting over the sanctuary of the Lord, exulting with her hands and stamping with her feet and rejoicing at what befell Jerusalem, things which Ezekiel did not see, since he was in the land of captivity, but the Lord revealed them to him. Therefore the Lord humbles her and delivers her to the men of the east [4], who exploit all her resources and make her capital “Rabbah” a stable for camels and all her cities a couching place for flocks [5].

25.2.1.en: In pride she gloated over the ruin of Judah and its affliction, and did not know that after five years Nebuchadnezzar would return and attack her and destroy her capital, the beautiful and rich city “Rabbah,” so that it would become a ruin, and the tribes would come from the east of Ammon, the Aramaean and Arab tribes, and use it as a stable for camels, and her cities would be turned into a couching place for flocks.

25.2.2.en: When a man exalts himself with pride he falls, and his splendor becomes a ruin and his heart becomes a pasture for animals: “flocks shall lie down in the midst of her, all the beasts of the nations” (Zeph 2:14). Man is changed from the gentle humanity in which he was created in the image and likeness of God into the rapacious, irrational animal nature. This is what pride did to King Belshazzar: he was driven from among men and his dwelling was with the beasts of the field, and his food the grass like oxen (Dan 4:25). For this reason the Fathers of the Church took great care to enjoy the spirit of humility and to flee from pride, until one of them said: “Do not dwell in a place that has a name, nor sit with a man of great name.” St. Basil the Great also said: [If you wish to be known to God, take care not to be known to men.] And Abba Timothy said: [If men honor you, fear greatly... flee from the honor of the many, lest they sink your ship.]

25.3.0.en: 8 “Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen; 9 Therefore, behold, I will open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities which are on his frontiers, the glory of the country, Bethjeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim, 10 Unto the men of the east with the Ammonites, and will give them in possession, that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations. 11 And I will execute judgments upon Moab; and they shall know that I am the LORD.

25.3.1.en: If the Ammonites are the offspring of Ben-ammi, the son of Lot by his younger daughter, then Moab is the son by his elder daughter, and he was so called because his mother bore him by her father Lot, so he was called Moab, that is, “from the father,” she having borne him by her father while he was in a state of drunkenness and unconsciousness. This is what led St. Jerome to consider that Moab refers to Satan and those who have departed from God their Father, who do not think of their Father.

25.3.2.en: The descendants of Moab spread out east of the Dead Sea and drove the Emims out from there (Deut 2:11), and they worshipped the god Chemosh. Their relationship with the Hebrews was sometimes good, for God commanded the Hebrews not to take their land (Deut 2:11), but most of the time the relationship was hostile; in the days of the Judges the Moabites subdued the Hebrews and laid tribute upon them until Ehud killed Eglon king of Moab (Judg 3:12-30), and Ruth, the girl who loved her mother-in-law, was a Moabite.

25.3.3.en: King Saul fought the Moabites, and when David fled from before him he placed his parents under their protection (1 Sam 22:3-4), but when he became king he struck them severely (2 Sam 8:2) and made them his servants. After the death of Solomon, Moab became part of the northern kingdom, and in the reign of Jehoshaphat they attacked Judea but were defeated before it (2 Kgs 3); after that Moab was sometimes subject and sometimes independent. And in the days of King Jehoiakim, Moab allied with the Chaldeans against Judah (2 Kgs 24:2).

25.3.4.en: In his prophecy against Moab he linked with it Seir [8], the center of the Edomites, because of their union in evil. It is to be noted that the word “Seir” is Hebrew and means “abundance of hair”; it was applied to the land which Esau, or Edom, and his offspring took from the Horites (Gen 32:3), and it was called Mount Seir because it is a mountainous region, situated on the eastern side of the Arabian wilderness, and it is Mount Seir which is in the land of Judah (Josh 15:10).

25.3.5.en: If the state of the Ammonites refers to the sin of pride, then Moab refers to “the spirit of lack of discernment”; she thought there was no difference between the living God and the pagan goddess, and reckoned from the destruction of Judah and the ruin of Jerusalem that there was no salvation for the people again: “They say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen” [8]. Therefore the Lord disciplines them by opening their fortified cities on the frontier, “Bethjeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim,” which are the secret of their strength, for the Chaldeans to shatter them and leave them in ruins; then the men of the east will come and use them for animals as they do with the Ammonites.

25.3.6.en: If the Ammonites lost their lives because of their pride, so the Moabites lose their lives because of lack of discernment. As St. Mar Ephrem the Syrian says: [Without clay the tower is not built; without knowledge no virtue stands.]

25.4.0.en: 12 “Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them; 13 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman; and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword. 14 And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel: and they shall do in Edom according to mine anger and according to my fury; and they shall know my vengeance, saith the Lord GOD.

25.4.1.en: “Edom” means “red” or “bloody (shedder of blood),” and it also means “from the earth”; therefore the sons of Edom refer to the shedding of blood or the sin of injustice.

25.4.2.en: “Edom” is the title of Esau, who was violent and bore enmity against his brother Jacob; this name was applied to the region where Esau dwelt, that is, to the land of Seir (Gen 32:3), a rugged mountainous region, which Esau and his offspring took after driving out the Horites (Deut 2:12). They did not permit the Hebrews to pass through their land after their exodus from Egypt (Num 20:14-21), although they were considered brothers to them (Deut 23:7-8). David invaded Edom and set garrisons over it (Num 24:18), and Hadad, one of the princes of Edom, fled to Egypt and became an adversary to Solomon (1 Kgs 11:14-22). In the days of Jehoshaphat the Edomites, the Ammonites and the Moabites invaded Judah, but they turned to fighting one another (2 Chr 20:1, 22, 23). The Edomites helped Israel and Judah in their war against Mesha king of Moab (2 Kgs 3:4-27), but they revolted in the days of the reign of Joram the son of Jehoshaphat, and he overcame them, but could not subdue them (2 Kgs 8:20; 1 Chr 21:8-10). Amaziah killed ten thousand of the Edomites, casting them down from the top of the rock, so that he killed them in the Valley of Salt, and took Selah, their capital, from them (2 Kgs 14:7; 2 Chr 25:11-12). The Edomites invaded the tribe of Judah and took captives from them during the reign of Ahaz... They rejoiced at Nebuchadnezzar’s destruction of Jerusalem (Ps 137:7). They also seized it as far as the city of Hebron. The prophets prophesied against it because of its intense enmity toward Israel, and they also prophesied of its incorporation into the Kingdom of God (Jer 49:7-22; Lam 4:21-22; Joel 3:19, etc.). In the fifth century B.C. the Nabataeans drove them out of Mount Seir, and in the second century B.C. Judas Maccabeus took Hebron and other cities that the Edomites had seized (1 Macc 5); John Hyrcanus compelled the Edomites to be circumcised and brought them into the community of the Jews, and Herod the Great was an Edomite.

25.5.0.en: If Edom refers to the sin of injustice and the shedding of blood, then with the measure with which it measures it will be measured. She took vengeance, and therefore the Lord says, “I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it” [13]. And he who kills with the sword will be killed with the sword. He has made it desolate from Teman in the north to Dedan in the south, where they fall by the sword.

25.6.0.en: 15 “Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because the Philistines have dealt by revenge, and have taken vengeance with a despiteful heart, to destroy it for the old hatred; 16 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will stretch out mine hand upon the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethims, and destroy the remnant of the sea coast. 17 And I will execute great vengeance upon them with furious rebukes; and they shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall lay my vengeance upon them.”

25.6.1.en: In the Old Testament the Philistines represented intense enmity toward the people of God, and St. Jerome interprets their name as “death by a poisonous draught”; therefore in his opinion they represented those who drink the cup of Satan’s seduction and fall quickly. They took vengeance on Judah like the sons of Edom, and perhaps the latter had incited them to it. In any case, Nebuchadnezzar defeated them not long after the fall of Jerusalem.

25.6.2.en: As for His cutting off the Cherethims, perhaps He meant by them a Philistine company who had come from the island of Crete in the first quarter of the twelfth century B.C.

25.6.3.en: The enmity between the Hebrews and the Philistines is ancient, from after the entrance of the former into the Promised Land, when they occupied some of their cities after the death of Joshua (Judg 1:18); but the Philistines recovered their cities and the Hebrews fell into their grasp (Judg 10:6-7), and then were rescued. The Philistines returned and humbled the Hebrews for forty years until Samson rescued them (Judg 14-16). In the time of the prophet Samuel they seized the Ark of the Covenant (1 Sam 4-6), and then Samuel defeated them after twenty years... They entered into war with the Hebrews in the days of King Saul, and King David took refuge with them twice, and when he reigned he fought them. After the death of David we do not hear much about them...

25.6.4.en: Shatter, O Lord, the corruption of the nations within me!

25.6.5.en: * I know Your love for all the children of men, for all nations!

25.6.6.en: What Your prophets prophesied was only to shatter the evil that is in me!

25.6.7.en: Who are the Ammonites but the pride that brings my soul down?!

25.6.8.en: Who are the sons of Moab but my rejection of Your fatherhood and my ascription to another father?!

25.6.9.en: Who are the Edomites but my violent, blood-shedding nature?!

25.6.10.en: Who are the ancient Philistines but the inward confusion?!

25.6.11.en: Shatter, O Lord, my corruption that I may be sanctified for You!

25.6.12.en: Remove my pride that I may enjoy Your humility!

25.6.13.en: Return me to Your fatherhood that I may leave the fatherhood of the devil!

25.6.14.en: Renew my stony heart that it may show compassion to everyone!

25.6.15.en: Remove all confusion within me that I may bear Your eternal peace!
